title: Two installs on one Tailscale machine share the machine link and invite with both locks
description: With only the tailscale command and the Tailscale API stubbed, up serves two fixture installs on their own ports (tailscale serve --bg --http=PORT), a rerun keeps the other install's route and a host without Tailscale gets one install instruction and carries on locally. Two served control planes on one simulated machine never read the host's machine directory: each install's master-loop sync carries the share link pasted on install A's Setup page (with the day it was made) into the shared machine record and back, so B shows it. Invite someone on each copies one message with that link and its own URL and port, saying the share reaches the machine as far as tailnet policy allows and each install needs its own sign-in; with no link saved the message is withheld and the missing step named. Invites redeem only on their own install, once, within 24 hours under a controlled clock; an older link keeps its real 30-day expiry, warns in its last seven days and refuses invites once expired. The optional API token is sealed to the host in the browser, written 0600 by the host alone, never shown, masked from confined sessions, and the host makes one single-use device invite through a fake Tailscale API before the Graphyard invite, failing whole when Tailscale refuses. No Docker or Tailscale credentials.
